statements.impact_statement: PCRE2 flaw needs an attacker-controlled pattern or subject; PCRE2 is only loaded by git (grep) which is not run. Checked in the v1.9.5 source and image build: the controller is a static Go binary (Dockerfile CGO_ENABLED=0) so it loads no system libraries; it has no os/exec in main.go, internal/ or fluxcd/pkg/kustomize v1.35.6 and kustomize plugins are disabled (DisabledPluginConfig). The only child process is git for kustomize remote bases (enabled, no --no-remote-bases), and no Kustomization uses one: every Kustomization sources the GitRepository talos-gitops and k8s/ on main has no remote resource URL. Holds while no remote base is added.

OpenSSL QUIC server flaw (unbounded queue for QUIC Initial packets) needs a QUIC/UDP listener. None exists and policy allows no UDP ingress; libssl is not linked into the Go binary. Policy: only TCP 8080/9440 listen; ingress only from kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and cluster on 8080; egress only DNS, kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and TCP 443 to github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, quay.io. GO-2026-5026: idna.ToASCII is linked, but the flaw only matters to code that authorizes on an ASCII hostname and later uses its Unicode form. The controller imports no x/net/idna and does no hostname-based authorization; idna is used only inside net/http name handling for the fixed peers (kube-apiserver, github.com, ghcr.io, quay.io). Policy: only TCP 8080/9440 listen; ingress only from kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and cluster on 8080; egress only DNS, kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and TCP 443 to github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, quay.io.
gdal infback9 bug matched to zlib by mistake; gdal is not in any image

CVE-2026-78661 is in x/net/html parsing. Not verified whether the binary links it. No untrusted HTML reaches this workload: default-deny CiliumNetworkPolicy, ingress only from kube-apiserver/node/cluster, egress only to named hosts (GitHub, ghcr, quay, Let's Encrypt, Cloudflare API). Fix: x/net v0.62.0 via Renovate.

govulncheck on usr/local/bin/kustomize-controller lists GO-2026-6609 (alias CVE-2026-78667, net/http Range handling in FileServer/ServeContent) only under Package Results: the package is imported but no vulnerable symbol is in the binary.

GO-2026-6611: HTTP/2 SETTINGS flood from a malicious peer; symbol is linked. As a server: the listeners are plain HTTP (no TLS) and no h2c handler exists in the controller source, so no HTTP/2 server. As a client: the only peers are the kube-apiserver and github.com/ghcr.io/quay.io over 443 and in-namespace pods. Policy: only TCP 8080/9440 listen; ingress only from kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and cluster on 8080; egress only DNS, kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and TCP 443 to github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, quay.io.

Needs a libcurl STARTTLS (SMTP/IMAP/POP3/FTP) transfer. Those ports are dropped by egress and libcurl is not used. Checked in the v1.9.5 source and image build: the controller is a static Go binary (Dockerfile CGO_ENABLED=0) so it loads no system libraries; it has no os/exec in main.go, internal/ or fluxcd/pkg/kustomize v1.35.6 and kustomize plugins are disabled (DisabledPluginConfig). Holds while no remote base is added.

grpc-go flaws (GO-2026-6348, GO-2026-6443, GO-2026-6061) are in the gRPC server transport and xDS server RBAC. The controller starts no gRPC server (no grpc.NewServer or xds.NewGRPCServer in main.go, internal/, fluxcd/pkg; the SOPS key service is an in-process local client, not a listener) and the listeners are plain HTTP on 8080 and 9440. As a gRPC client it could only reach the allowed hosts, which do not serve gRPC. Policy: only TCP 8080/9440 listen; ingress only from kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and cluster on 8080; egress only DNS, kube-apiserver, same-namespace pods and TCP 443 to github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, quay.io.
